capability.summary: Run npm audit --json for one local project and return its report envelope
capability.description: Invokes `npm audit --json --prefix <project_dir>` where a directory input is used directly and a file input contributes its parent directory. npm exit codes 0 and 1 are treated as completed audits, and parsed npm JSON is returned in `result`; no report file is exported.
capability.problem_space: Read-only invocation of npm's dependency advisory audit for a local lockfile-backed project; not vulnerability remediation, package installation, static source scanning, offline CVE lookup, or JSON report-file export.

env_requirements: a usable npm registry/network configuration and a supported lockfile in the resolved project directory
constraint.io_signature: Input: required file_path string naming an existing project directory or file such as package.json; files resolve to their absolute parent directory. Executes `npm audit --json --prefix <dir>`. Output: uniform JSON execution envelope with parsed report in result when npm emits one.
accepted_inputs: an existing file path whose parent directory is the intended npm project, typically package.json
constraint.output_shape: npm exit 0 or 1: {status: "success", tool: "npm", target: string, exit_code: 0|1, result: object|array|scalar|null, stdout: string|null, stderr: string|null}. The helper tries to parse stdout first and stderr second; whenever either stream parses as one non-null JSON value, result receives it and stdout is set to null. Thus non-JSON stdout is discarded from the envelope when stderr supplies parseable JSON, while stderr still retains its original text. Other npm exits use status="tool_error" and propagate the exit code. Missing input, executable, or 180-second timeout yields {status: "error", tool: "npm", message: string}, exiting 2/3/4. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON.
limitations: does not run `npm audit fix`, install packages, modify manifests intentionally, or export a report file; it only invokes npm audit and returns its output
audit findings and report schema depend on npm version, registry advisory state, lockfile contents, network availability, authentication, and configuration, so results are nondeterministic
file inputs are not verified to be package.json and simply select their parent directory; npm decides project validity

uses a fixed 180-second timeout with no output truncation; if stdout is non-JSON but stderr is JSON, stderr is parsed into result and the helper still forces stdout=null, losing the original non-JSON stdout

output_contract.description: JSON execution envelope containing npm's parsed audit report when available, raw streams otherwise, and npm exit metadata; no report file is written.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: run npm audit and capture its JSON report
inspect npm lockfile dependencies for registry advisories
negative_intents: install update or remove npm packages
export an npm audit report file
scan JavaScript source code for security bugs
